alignments.note: Finite verb with its subject pronoun under rule 17.

Construct noun with a supplied *the*: the ASV renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before each noun, so nothing is fronted and each takes the one standing before its own word, under rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's *of* under rule 19, discontinuous around its own article under rule 25.
Article on the rectum takes the *the* standing before its own word, under rule 29's arthrous count.
Verb rendered by a light verb with its complement; rule 44 heads it on *pleasure*, and the unit is discontinuous around the negative determiner under rule 25.
The ASV recasts the clause's negation onto the object nominal; the negative takes the determiner that negation has become, under rule 15.
Construct noun with the supplied *the* under rule 29, the rectum being rendered indefinitely so that nothing is fronted.
The ASV writes *a man* for the rectum, an indefinite rendering that determines the word already, so this article morpheme has no written *the* and is `unrepresented` under rule 29.
Nomen rectum takes the chain's *of* under rule 19 and its own indefinite article under rule 15.
